subject: Preflight: on-prem deployment runbook + gap analysis (node pools & storage)

Subject: Preflight: on-prem deployment runbook + gap analysis (node pools & storage)

Samantha — good to meet you earlier. As discussed, we want to align on a short preflight checklist so we can produce a focused on-prem runbook and node/storage plan for your pilot cluster. I attached a lightweight preflight template to capture the items below; if you can fill the sheet it will speed up the sizing pass.

Top-level asks (high priority):
- Cluster footprint: expected minimum/peak concurrent requests for model inferencing (tokens/sec or qps) and batch sizing targets.
- Rack & host profiles: CPU, RAM, GPU type (if any), local NVMe vs network SSD per host.
- Storage expectations: PV classes available (NFS, Ceph/RBD, iSCSI), expected PV sizes, typical IOPS and throughput per volume, backup windows and RPO/RTO targets.
- Network: VLANs/subnets we can use for control plane, data plane, and management; egress constraints; firewall / proxy rules for Redwoods services.
- KMS/PKI: do you have a customer-managed KMS/HSM we can integrate for secrets and disk encryption?
- Compliance: any additional logging/audit requirements (retention, SIEM ingestion).
- Maintenance window preferences and approved escalation contacts.

Extras that help but aren't blockers: kernel version, container runtime, CNI, and existing monitoring stack access.

Attachments: preflight-template.xlsx (simple tabular form).

Can you and your ops lead populate the sheet by EOD Wednesday? If we need a technical sync I can ask Dev to join — slot availability: 10/28 14:00–16:00 PST.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Preflight: on-prem deployment runbook + gap analysis (node pools & storage)

Hi Priya — thanks for the note and the template. I populated the sheet and attached our inventory and a quick network sketch. High level answers below; see attached CSV for host-by-host details.

- Cluster footprint: pilot will be a single 8-node cluster. Typical inference load today is ~120 qps (CPU models), spike to 350 qps expected during clinic hours. Ave token length low (~30 tokens). We plan to start without GPUs and add a GPU pool if latency doesn't meet targets.
- Rack & host profiles: hosts are Dell R750xl, 2 x AMD Genoa 64c, 1TB RAM, local NVMe (1.6 TB) on each host. No GPUs initially.
- Storage expectations: we currently expose an on-prem Ceph RBD cluster and an NFS export for shared data. RBD volumes typically 1–4 TB, 5k–20k IOPS depending on pool. Backup via our Veeam job nightly; RPO 4 hours for primary data, 24 hours for logs.
- Network: we can provision separate subnets for control and data plane. Egress to public internet is NATed through a proxy; we may need help with proxy TLS interception for downloads.
- KMS/PKI: We have an internal Vault cluster (HashiCorp Vault) with HSM-backed auto-unseal. We can create a test service account for you.
- Compliance: we ship audit logs to Splunk; retention 12 months. We can provide an ingestion token and a test index.
- Maintenance windows: weekdays 01:00–04:00 local. Primary ops: me (samantha.lee@novahealth.com), secondary: infra-team@novahealth.com.

Questions for Redwood:
1) For model shard caching / KV cache, do you rely on local NVMe per node or do you recommend network-attached fast volumes?
2) What's your recommended default PVC class mapping for model weights vs logs vs ephemeral KV?

Attachments: nova-infra-inventory.csv (csv), network-diagram.png (png).

Happy to do the sync on 10/28 at 14:30 if that works.

Best,

Samantha Lee
Ops Lead, Nova Health

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <ops-lead@novahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: on-prem deployment runbook + gap analysis (node pools & storage)

Thanks Samantha — the inventory is great. Quick notes from a runtime/architecture POV and a short proposal attached: nodepool-sizing-proposal.md and PV class mapping.

Summary recommendations (pilot phase):
- Node pools:
  * system/control-plane: 3 dedicated masters (customer-managed control plane is fine; we recommend HA control plane isolated on management VLAN).
  * infra: 2 nodes, 32vCPU / 256GB RAM, no GPUs — run logging, monitoring (Prom/Thanos), ingress controllers, and Ceph client daemons. Tolerations: infra=true.
  * inference-cpu: 5 nodes, 64vCPU / 512GB RAM each, local NVMe used for model cache (fast ephemeral). Tolerations: workload=inference.
  Note: we picked 5 inference nodes to handle your 350 qps spike with headroom; we'll re-run sizing once you enable GPU pool.

- Storage mapping:
  * model-weights: local NVMe-backed PVCs (ReadMostly, ephemeral) for model shards and KV cache — we recommend tmpfs for very hot state and NVMe for warm cache.
  * persistent-state: RBD volumes for long-term stores (1–4TB); set reclaimPolicy=Retain and snapshot schedule daily.
  * logs/metrics: NFS share (or CephFS) with dedicated retention lifecycle into your Splunk index.

- IOPS and throughput guidance:
  * model cache per node: expect 1500–3000 IOPS sustained per NVMe device; tune read ahead and fio test during pilot.
  * PVC accessMode: use ReadWriteOnce for model volumes to keep locality.

- Kubernetes tuning:
  * kubelet: --kube-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi --system-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi for inference nodes; evictionHard set to memory.available<200Mi.
  * kubelet churn: disable dynamic Kubelet config; set pod-eviction-timeout to 5m during pilot.
  * CNI: Calico with IPIP disabled is fine — ensure MTU matches host NICs.

- Security/KMS:
  * We can integrate with your Vault via Kubernetes auth + CSI secrets driver for disk encryption keys. Need a service account with read/write to a specific path.

Next steps:
1) We'll produce a short runbook with helm charts, PV class YAML, and a nodepool sizing spreadsheet by 2026-11-04.
2) Priya to own the runbook and validation plan; Nova to provide a test Vault service account and one host with fio access for IO validation.

Attachments: nodepool-sizing-proposal.md (md), pv-class-mapping.yaml (yaml). I pasted a small excerpt of the PV class mapping below for quick copy: 

# PV class excerpt
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: rbd-fast
provisioner: rook-ceph.rbd.csi.ceph.com
parameters:
  pool: fast-pool
  imageFormat: "2"
reclaimPolicy: Retain
mountOptions:
  - discard
  - noatime

Let us know if you want us to convert any Ceph RBD volumes to raw devices for perf testing.

-Dev
